summary: All 1,398 www tests pass with 91.95% line coverage. The merged blog validation loses a kept check. The contrast check can pass unreadable text.
blocking_findings: F22 [Blocker] phase-acceptance: The ADV-8 remediation skips dot-prefixed .md files at fixtures/blog-posts-loader.ts:57. The same en/.phase-three-probe.md input fails the phase-base URL-safe slug rule by name. All 17 merged cases pass at the audited HEAD. Production blog.ts:79–85 and 294–299 still discover and count that filename. Restore the kept check for every production-discoverable .md file.

F23 [Blocker] phase-acceptance: The F21 remediation resolves remaining var() values from a global map, not the element, at fixtures/contrast.ts:64–72 and 285–290. A pricing title with an inline --color-slate-900 of #faf9f7 on the same background passes at 16.97:1. The equivalent literal color fails at 1:1. Use the effective custom property or fail when it cannot be determined.
nonblocking_findings: F24 [Nit] phase-acceptance: The initial R2 rewrite of hero-section.test.tsx:52–56 checks only that two gradient stops exist. Changing the middle and end stops to white and amber passes all seven cases. The former class pins rejected this change. This is a late finding outside the remediation lines.
evidence: Git confirms the exact phase base 8a126f612abcc258c6c6711d6ac03fa085bbcbff and the unchanged audited HEAD 704745a3ca2bb27b52f28e2fcf65df9d994b64ac. The role base equals the audited HEAD.

The Phase 2 acceptance artifact passes at the Phase 3 base. Green, final Review A, and final adversarial testing all target 704745a3c. No test-only exception is needed between those results and acceptance.
Review B, Review C, and UX browser review do not apply under test-strategy.md:78–87. No browser ran.
All 10 Phase 3 tasks have [x] and a resolvable first-line SHA. Tasks 3.1 and 3.3 cite the phase base because classification.md has no R1 or R3 rows.
The R2 inventory has 16 cases. The R2 commit changes nine files and covers 14 cases. plan.md:272–276 identifies the two previously rewritten cases and the F11 approval.

The seven class, merge, and remediation receipts match the labeled GREEN and COVERAGE logs. The four exit fields are zero in each receipt. Line coverage is 91.60%, 91.60%, 91.64%, 91.76%, 91.83%, 91.93%, and 91.95%. The floor is 85.52%.
The class and remediation lint logs record zero errors and three warnings. The type logs show tsc --noEmit with no diagnostics. Fresh type check and lint both exit 0 at the audited HEAD.
The fresh heavy-run test:coverage exits 0: 95 files and 1,398 tests pass. V8 reports 91.95% lines, or 1,611 of 1,752. The baseline also has Markdown remap warnings.

All nine proof-r2 logs contain assertion failures and exit 1. The paired F19, F20, and F21 logs also contain assertion failures and exit 1. The proofs cover their named mutations, not all forms of a regression.

The blog merge reduces 1,726 cases to 17. Its three recorded post mutations exit 1 and name en/1-district-1-quality-school. A fresh blank-author probe also exits 1 and names that post and the author rule.

The same dot-prefixed Markdown entry gives 17 passes at the audited HEAD and one named slug failure with 1,739 passes at the phase base. The initial merge still loaded it. Commit 98c2713d3 added the skip.

An in-memory pricing probe logs var(--color-slate-900) and a computed custom property of #faf9f7. The helper substitutes rgb(15,23,42) and reports 16.97:1. The literal control gives 1:1 and fails the WCAG check.
F22 concerns a line added by the ADV-8 remediation. F23 concerns the foreground resolution line changed by the F21 remediation. F24 concerns the original R2 rewrite.
The Git range has no non-test, non-Measure path and no changed blog post. The probes were in memory. No tracked file needed restoration.

A5: The plan's recorded command exits agree with the runner output. The task 3.5 statement that every post receives validation does not hold after ADV-8. A3, A4, A6, and A7 do not apply to the unchanged Measure framework.

The raw reduction from 3,175 to 1,398 is 55.97%, which rounds to 56%. The named breakage proofs are valid for their inputs. Do not credit the merge toward acceptance while it weakens the K row. Excluding the 1,709-case merge reduction leaves 3,107 cases and a 2.14% reduction.
